body:
> I see some type of fallback has been implemented via https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8006 but it seems not to be working in this case.

> D3D12 11_0 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: Intel - Intel(R) HD Graphics 4600

The problem with current fallback system, it is done in an early stage of renderer initialization, and only works if API is completely missing (e.g, DX12→GL should work on Windows 7). Windows 10+ always have some level of DX12 support. It's running with `11.0` feature level, which is insufficient for Godot, but renderer init still works, and fallback doesn't trigger.

Godot can work with DX12 11_*  as long as they support SM6.1 (some older Intel GPUs actually do this and their Vulkan support is not that good anyway). 
The issue at hand here is #98207 but I currently do not have the time to do a proper pull request for this one. Older SM cannot be supported due with the approach Godot took for DirectX support.

Thanks for the context.

On this device, Godot 4.4 refuses to create a new project with Forward+. Does that imply there is a codepath there that is detecting that D3D12 is not usable? If so, I wonder if we can use it (or get inspiration from it) here.

I also had a user reporting something similar on windows (running on i3-3120M), the exported godot 4.4.1 game crashes with the following log:

```
Godot Engine v4.4.1.stable.official.49a5bc7b6 - https://godotengine.org
WARNING: Your video card drivers seem not to support Vulkan, switching to Direct3D 12.
   at: DisplayServerWindows (platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:6831)
ERROR: D3D12CreateDevice failed with error 0x887a0004.
   at: _initialize_device (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:6381)
ERROR: Condition "err != OK" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_CREATE
   at: initialize (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:6747)
ERROR: Failed to initialize driver for device.
   at: initialize (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:6657)
```

But shouldn't the engine try to fall back to openGL after it tried d3d12? It doesn't seem to do this here, probably because that attempt crashes the game...

I had to disable d3d12 fallback in my project for now (with angle and opengl fallback still active), then the game works just fine.

I have a Windows 10 user I think is running into a similar or related issue where an exported 4.4.1 Mobile renderer project crashes at startup. 

The log starts with: 
```
Godot Engine v4.4.1.stable.official.49a5bc7b6 - https://godotengine.org
vkEnumerateInstanceVersion not available, assuming Vulkan 1.0.
ERROR: Required extension VK_KHR_surface not found.
   at: _initialize_instance_extensions (drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:487)
ERROR: Condition "err != OK" is true. Returning: err
   at: initialize (drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:928)
WARNING: Your video card drivers seem not to support Vulkan, switching to Direct3D 12.
   at: DisplayServerWindows (platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:6831)
D3D12 11_0 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA Quadro K1200
WARNING: PSO caching is not implemented yet in the Direct3D 12 driver.
   at: pipeline_cache_create (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:4944)
ERROR: Shader translation at stage Compute failed.
   at: shader_compile_binary_from_spirv (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:3321)
ERROR: Condition "shader_data.is_empty()" is true.
   at: _compile_variant (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp:344)
ERROR: Shader translation at stage Compute failed.
   at: shader_compile_binary_from_spirv (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:3321)
ERROR: Condition "shader_data.is_empty()" is true.
   at: _compile_variant (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp:344)
ERROR: Shader translation at stage Compute failed.
   at: shader_compile_binary_from_spirv (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:3321)
ERROR: Condition "shader_data.is_empty()" is true.
   at: _compile_variant (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp:344)
```

Followed by a lot of errors that seem related to shader compiling, and ending in:

```
ERROR: Parameter "shader" is null.
   at: uniform_set_create (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:3432)
ERROR: Parameter "pipeline" is null.
   at: draw_list_bind_render_pipeline (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4424)
ERROR: Parameter "uniform_set" is null.
   at: draw_list_bind_uniform_set (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4520)
```


In this case it seems like it's correctly seeing Vulkan isn't supported and trying to fall back to Direct3D 12, however in this case it seems to get a D3D12 driver up, only it's not working at all and all the shader compilation fails and then the project crashes at some point. So maybe in this case it should also have failed starting up Direct3D and fallen back to OpenGL?

_EDIT: Eventually it seems this was fixed by the user updating their graphics card drivers, so might have been a driver bug. But even so I'm leaving this here since I think it should have failed more gracefully with an error message and fallback to OpenGL instead of crashing silently._

> Godot can work with DX12 11_* as long as they support SM6.1

So you're saying that the D3D12 renderer doesn't work with Shader Model 6.0? The code seems to imply that 6.0 is compatible. If not, that's important to determine for handling fallbacks.
